parsed.explanation: A pending but widely expected law criminalises identifying as transgender (up to 3 years) and cross-dressing, with a duty to report, atop existing 'unnatural carnal knowledge' (up to 3 years), documented mob justice, and a national-security raid/closure of LGBTQ organisations in the capital. No legal gender recognition or anti-discrimination protection, no documented visitor-specific entry, custody or care rules, and no enforcement record yet for the 2026 bill. Post-outing imprisonment is therefore a credible statutory threat with societal violence and no documented recourse, but custodial torture, routine visitor arrest, or execution are not documented.

entry_documents.exposure: No traveller-specific entry, visa or airport screening rule documented; unresolved whether identification/cross-dressing offences apply to short-term visitors.
entry_documents.interaction: If assented and applied to visitors, document/presentation mismatch could trigger the identification offence and duty-to-report.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Pending bill provides up to 3 years for identifying as transgender and longer for promotion; no prison-placement rule for trans people documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. Paralegal initiative for residents noted.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement and conditions if detained are unknown; do not assume safety from silence.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, ward or public-facility rule for visitors documented.

care_services.exposure: No visitor care, HRT import or emergency-care rule documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: 2026 bill passed unanimously in 2024 form and again May 2026, awaiting expected assent; criminalises identification as transgender, promotion, cross-dressing per sources, and imposes duty to report. Existing law up to 3 years.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Judicial review deferred until assent; no operative protection documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Religious/political pressure and prior national-security raid show enforcement actors aligned against LGBTQ presence.

minors_guardians.exposure: No age-specific rule for travelling minors or guardians documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Promotion/advocacy and duty-to-report provisions could be argued to reach accompanying minors, but application undocumented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Mob justice against perceived LGBT people documented; capital LGBTQ centre forced to close and rights office raided by national security in 2021; groups operate secretly/online.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented police protection for trans victims; no anti-discrimination protection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: State closure/raid corroborates societal hostility and weakens recourse if outing leads to mob or police action.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Supreme court dismissed challenges as premature before assent; no visitor remedy, entry rule, custody practice or 2026 enforcement record documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Petitioners' lawyers exploring further options; resident paralegal initiative only.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of documentation in a thin, hostile structural context resolves toward risk, not neutrality.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: raids, fines/short detention, no execution, weak recourse. This case is similar or slightly lower because a 3-year identification offence is legislated (pending) rather than rare, but no routine visitor detention/extortion pattern is documented.

Lower severity: 0.15-A has routine arrests, months of pretrial custody, custodial beatings and illusory appeals. Here custodial abuse and routine visitor arrest are not documented, and the 2026 bill/counts are not yet in force, so higher than 0.15.
Higher severity: 0.35-A is exclusion/humiliation without imprisonment. Here the statutory consequence for identifying as transgender is imprisonment, plus mob justice, so materially below 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: national pending criminalisation of transgender identification and existing sexuality law, reinforced by documented mob justice and a security raid on LGBTQ infrastructure, create a credible post-outing imprisonment and violence threat with no documented visitor protections or remedies. Mitigating that it is not yet assented, visitor application is unresolved, and no custodial torture, organised visitor sweeps or capital penalty are documented, placing it above the 0.15 tier but below administrative-exclusion cases around 0.35.
